headline: High-risk workflow automation can write shared files and invoke broad networked integrations, while RisingWave is network-isolated; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are the main concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate tools via workflow nodes, so attacker-controlled content can be routed into downstream steps. RisingWave has no documented input channel here, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than directly evidenced; uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF n8n workflows ingest untrusted file contents and pass them into AI Agent or code nodes
IF RisingWave outputs are copied into n8n workflow inputs without provenance checks
mitigations: Add explicit content provenance labels before any AI Agent node
Insert a manual approval step before executing instructions from files
Restrict n8n workflows to trusted directories only
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and can egress broadly through integrations, so sensitive workflow data may leave the server. RisingWave is documented as network-egress none, which reduces leakage from B but does not prevent A from exporting data; the shared-data path is plausible enough for medium severity.
conditions: IF n8n workflows process secrets, customer data, or regulated records
IF any n8n integration node sends those records to an external API
mitigations: Limit n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes
Disable or review outbound integrations for sensitive workflows
Separate sensitive workflows into a dedicated n8n instance
requires-engineering: add DLP or field-level redaction before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server filesystem write and broad integration access, but RisingWave exposes no writable surface or mutable shared resource in the profile. With no documented overlapping write target, a direct capability conflict is not established; the remaining risk is limited and mostly hypothetical.
conditions: IF both systems are configured to write to the same external database or bucket
IF an orchestrator maps n8n outputs into a mutable RisingWave-adjacent resource
mitigations: Assign separate storage targets per system
Lock down shared credentials to read-only where possible
Review workflow destinations before enabling writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can act on AI Agent outputs through workflow nodes, so if RisingWave-derived data is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated actions. RisingWave itself is not shown to verify or correct those outputs, so the interaction is inferred and medium severity fits the default automation pathway.
conditions: IF n8n uses RisingWave data as an input to an AI Agent or decision node
IF downstream workflow nodes execute emails, tickets, or database writes without human review
mitigations: Add validation steps before any action-taking node
Require human approval for high-impact workflow branches
Log source data and generated actions side by side
requires-engineering: implement schema checks on RisingWave-fed inputs

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for RisingWave, while n8n stores secrets on its server and processes whatever the workflow handles. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced for both agents, this is a low-confidence, low-severity gap rather than a demonstrated breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through n8n workflows without a matching retention policy
IF the deployment places n8n in a jurisdiction that conflicts with the data class
mitigations: Document data classes allowed in each workflow
Review retention settings for n8n credential and execution logs
Restrict regulated data to approved workflows only
